claims.text: Pulumi's component state migrations let component authors ship an upgrade path with the component itself.
A Pulumi component state migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
Pulumi's component state migrations are new (recently introduced).
The Pulumi component state migrations API is experimental and may change.
A GitHub discussion exists at pulumi/pulumi discussions/24799 for component state migrations feedback.
A Pulumi docs page exists at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/components/state-migrations/ covering the component state migrations callback contract.
The pulumi/examples repo contains an aws-ts-awsx-vpc-state-migration example with three programs (v1, v2, v3) and the migration code.
Components link to /docs/iac/concepts/components/ and Aliases link to /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/aliases/ exist as docs pages.
The v1 example uses the legacy `awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc` component, which creates a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and its association, and an internet gateway.
In the example, a security group sits outside the VPC component and refers to the VPC.
Because the security group refers to the VPC's ID, replacing the VPC would require replacing the security group (AWS EC2 security group VpcId property change forces replacement).
The example does not create a database.
A replacement database does not automatically contain the old database's data.
The second version of the example upgrades to the modern `awsx.ec2.Vpc` component while keeping the existing network.
The third version removes AWSX and declares the resources directly with `@pulumi/aws`.
Across all three versions of the example, the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.

In the example, the v1 resource tree is awsx:x:ec2:Vpc with children aws Vpc, awsx:x:ec2:Subnet (containing subnet, route table, association named vpc-isolated-0) and awsx:x:ec2:InternetGateway; v2 is awsx:ec2:Vpc with aws Vpc parent of subnet vpc-isolated-1, route table, association and internet gateway; v3 is plain aws Vpc with the same children.
Each Pulumi state record has a Pulumi name called a URN, and managed resources also have an ID from the cloud provider.
The legacy AWSX component wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components, while modern AWSX removes those wrappers and puts managed resources under different parents.
In the example, the Pulumi name of the subnet changes from `vpc-isolated-0` to `vpc-isolated-1` between legacy and modern AWSX.
Pulumi aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when its saved state remains compatible.
Aliases alone cannot remove component wrappers and transfer references to the resources that take their place; a state migration can describe that whole change together.
Pulumi resource registration accepts a `stateMigrations` option that takes migration callbacks, and an alias for the legacy component type can be registered alongside it.
`migrateClassicVpc` comes from the example's v2/migration.ts file in pulumi/examples.
The alias lets Pulumi find the old component; the migration callback receives the old component's saved state followed by the state of its children.

A state migration callback returns `newState` (the complete set of records that replace the old component and its children) and `successors` (a map from each old URN that disappears to the URN that takes its place).
In the example's migration callback, if state already uses modern AWSX or plain AWS resources it does nothing, and an unexpected component type raises an error.
The example's `rename` helper copies the saved record, changes its URN, type, and parent, and preserves the AWS resource ID and other saved fields.
The `successors` entries let the Pulumi engine update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack, keeping the security group's reference to the VPC valid after migration.
The third version of the example declares the VPC, subnet, route table, association, and internet gateway directly with `@pulumi/aws`.
The second migration removes the AWSX VPC component record and moves the managed VPC into its place; both the old component and its VPC child map to the new VPC record, and the VPC keeps its AWS ID.
The second migration is located at v3/migration.ts in the pulumi/examples aws-ts-awsx-vpc-state-migration example.
The VPC registration in the v3 example keeps aliases for both previous component types and both migration callbacks.
Pulumi runs multiple state migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next callback.
A stack still using legacy AWSX can upgrade directly to the plain AWS version, and a stack already using modern AWSX skips the first migration.
Once both migrations have run, both callbacks return no result on later updates.
Keeping earlier migrations with the component means users can skip versions without editing stack state by hand.
After a migration changes saved state, Pulumi compares the new program with that state and calls the provider for any remaining changes.
In the example, upgrades can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags even though resource IDs are kept.
During the example upgrades, `pulumi preview` should show no creates, deletes, or replacements for the existing VPC, subnet, route table, association, internet gateway, and security group.
`pulumi preview` evaluates the state migration without saving it, and `pulumi up` saves the migrated state.
The example's v1 directory has a README to follow, and the same stack, backend, project name, AWS region, and availability zone must be used for each version.

When a component author registers the migration inside the component implementation, users do not need to write the migration, attach the callback, or edit stack state; Pulumi runs the migration as part of the normal preview and update.
For an internal component change that keeps the same inputs and outputs, users can keep their existing component calls.
Pulumi state migration callbacks (the state migrations resource option) run during previews and updates when prior state exists.
Pulumi state migration callbacks must be idempotent.
Pulumi state migration callbacks should return no result when the state no longer needs migration.
Pulumi state migration callbacks rewrite state without performing provider operations.
A Pulumi component state migration is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.
A Pulumi component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings.
In a Pulumi component state migration result, each successor mapping connects an old URN omitted from the result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, a Pulumi component state migration callback returns no result.
The option reference for the stateMigrations resource option, at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/statemigrations/#callback-api, explains the callback API.

Component state migration state entries use the checkpoint resource format documented in the Pulumi developer docs deployment schema (pulumi-resource-state), including fields such as urn, type, id, parent, provider, inputs, and outputs.
A component state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using update plans or targeted updates.
The restrictions on state-changing results of component state migrations (with update plans or targeted updates) do not require removing an already-applied migration.
